why: Personal Microsoft account: outlook.com, hotmail.com, xbox.com and account.microsoft.com all send the password to login.live.com (Microsoft identity platform overview: personal Microsoft accounts cover Skype, Xbox and Outlook.com). Apple lists live.com, hotmail.com and microsoft.com together only in shared-credentials-historical.json. account.microsoft.com is named as a host because microsoft.com also serves work and school sign-in.

login.microsoftonline.com (the common and consumers endpoints) and office.com sign in personal Microsoft accounts as well as work or school accounts (Microsoft identity platform protocols doc: common takes both, consumers takes Microsoft accounts), so a personal login is offered there. A login saved there may be a work or school account, which login.live.com doesn't take, so it never goes the other way.
office.com hands its sign-in to login.microsoftonline.com, which takes every account office.com does.
